# core/spancmp.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/spancmp.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Comparing two pieces of a text in byte order.

What is proved: `span_cmp` returns -1, 0 or 1, and says through `span_le`
which of the two comes first, and that 0 means the same bytes. `span_le`
is opaque outside this file (see the comment on it), so the sorting
module (core/strsort.bastio) reasons about it as an unknown relation that
`span_cmp` decides.

`import "core/spancmp.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`span_cmp`](#span_cmp) | Compares two spans of `b` in byte order. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `span_cmp`

```bastio
fn span_cmp(b: &Bytes, x: Span, y: Span) -> i8
  requires span_in(x, b) && span_in(y, b)
  ensures result == -1 || result == 0 || result == 1
  ensures result <= 0 ==> span_le(b, x.start, x.end, y.start, y.end)
  ensures result >= 0 ==> span_le(b, y.start, y.end, x.start, x.end)
  ensures result == 0 ==> x.end - x.start == y.end - y.start && bytes_same_at(b, x.start, b, y.start, x.end - x.start)
```

Compares two spans of `b` in byte order: -1 if `x` is smaller, 0 if they
hold the same bytes, 1 if `x` is larger.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("applepie");
let apple = Span { start: 0, end: 5 };
let pie = Span { start: 5, end: 8 };
let app = Span { start: 0, end: 3 };
let ok = span_cmp(b, apple, pie) == -1 && span_cmp(b, pie, apple) == 1
  && span_cmp(b, app, apple) == -1 && span_cmp(b, apple, apple) == 0;
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `span_lex`

```bastio
spec fn span_lex(b: &Bytes, xs: u64, xe: u64, ys: u64, ye: u64) -> bool {
  (forall p: u64 :: p < xe - xs && p < ye - ys && bytes_same_at(b, xs, b, ys, p)
     && bget(b, xs + p) != bget(b, ys + p) ==> bget(b, xs + p) < bget(b, ys + p))
  && (xe - xs <= ye - ys || !bytes_same_at(b, xs, b, ys, ye - ys))
}
```

The span `xs..xe` of `b` is at or before `ys..ye` in byte order: at every
position where the two agree up to there and both have a byte, the byte
of the first is not larger, and the second is not a proper prefix of the
first.

### `span_le`

```bastio
opaque spec fn span_le(b: &Bytes, xs: u64, xe: u64, ys: u64, ye: u64) -> bool {
  span_lex(b, xs, xe, ys, ye)
}
```

`span_lex`, opaque outside this file: a caller knows it only from the
contracts below. (Inside quantifiers over vectors the solver handles an
uninterpreted function far better than the inlined body.)
